hunks.baseline: Looking back now, I suppose all of it was just growing pains. But that was how it was back then.
hunks.sol: Looking back, I suppose it was all growing pains. But that was how it was back then.

hunks.baseline: It was only natural. At the time, I was a newly minted adult still wet behind the ears, and the Hunter training camp was literally nothing more than a training camp.
hunks.sol: It was only natural. I had barely reached adulthood, and the Hunter training camp was just that: a training camp.

hunks.baseline: What had my first real mission been like?
hunks.sol: What was my first real fight like?

hunks.baseline: No matter how hard I tried to remember, the memory remained hazy as fog.
Not because it had passed its expiration date, but because I had half-lost my mind the moment the battle began.
hunks.sol: No matter how hard I try to remember, it’s hazy as fog. Not because the memory has faded with age, but because I half-lost my mind the moment the battle began.

hunks.baseline: Of course, a few fragments had remained clear.
hunks.sol: A few fragments remain clear.

hunks.baseline: The backs of the tanks collapsing beneath the monsters’ overwhelming numbers. The thick stench of blood and the foul odor of creatures that did not belong to this world.
hunks.sol: The backs of the tanks as they buckled under the sheer number of monsters. The thick stench of blood and the reek of creatures that didn’t belong to this world.

hunks.baseline: The weight of the spear that had felt heavier than ever, and my sweat-soaked grip around it…
hunks.sol: The spear feeling heavier than it ever had before. Sweat pooling in my grip…

hunks.baseline: That was all.
At the moment of impact, everything around me had grown distant. When I opened my eyes again, the world was a sea of blood.
hunks.sol: That was all. The moment we clashed, everything around me seemed to recede. When I came to, there was blood everywhere.

hunks.baseline: And the Team Leader, who had been waiting for me to wake up with a cigarette between his lips, had immediately said this:
hunks.sol: The Team Leader had been waiting for me to wake up, a cigarette between his lips. The first thing he said was:

hunks.baseline: “I almost died saving your ass. Did my wife put you up to it? Tell you to kill me and split the insurance payout with her?”
hunks.sol: “I almost died saving your ass. Did my wife put you up to it? Tell you to kill me so you two could split the insurance payout?”

hunks.baseline: “You fought pretty well for someone who’d lost his mind, but if you pull that shit again, you’re going to die. Seriously.”
hunks.sol: “You fought pretty well for someone who’d lost his mind, but pull that shit again and you’re going to die. Seriously.”

hunks.baseline: “Holy shit. People were born in 2000?”
hunks.sol: “Fuck. People were still being born in 2020?”

hunks.baseline: The Team Leader had glared at me while puffing furiously on his cigarette. Only then did he tell me his name.
hunks.sol: The Team Leader glared at me, puffing hard on his cigarette. Only then did he tell me his name.

hunks.baseline: “From now on, when we’re off duty, calling me uncle would be a little weird. Call me hyung instead. Cheonsu hyung.”
hunks.sol: “From now on, when we’re off duty, call me… Uncle? No, that’s a bit much. Call me hyung. Cheonsu hyung.”

hunks.baseline: “This kid doesn’t even know how to refuse politely. And we’re still inside the Gate, you little shit.”
hunks.sol: “This kid doesn’t even pretend to refuse. And we’re still inside the Gate, you little shit.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know it at the time.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know it then.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know that I would share thick and thin like brothers with that Team Leader who looked so foul-tempered.

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know that, only a few years later, he would sacrifice himself in my place.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know that I’d come to share thick and thin like a brother with that foul-tempered Team Leader. Or that, only a few years later, he would sacrifice himself for me.

hunks.baseline: Six 50,000-won bills, after taxes and the Guild’s fee had been deducted.
hunks.sol: Six 50,000-won bills, after taxes and the Guild’s fee.

hunks.baseline: I took the payment for risking my life that day and returned to my goshiwon.[^1]
hunks.sol: I took my pay for risking my life that day and went back to my goshiwon.[^1]

hunks.baseline: When I opened the door, the room—less than four pyeong—smelled of mold. A family photograph sat on a table with a broken corner.
hunks.sol: When I opened the door, the room—less than four pyeong—smelled of mold. A family photograph sat on a table with a chipped corner.

hunks.baseline: At first, I only sobbed quietly. But before long, I buried my face between my knees and wailed like a little child.
hunks.sol: At first, I sobbed quietly. Before long, I had buried my face between my knees and was bawling like a child.

hunks.baseline: “Hey, new guy. Sorry for barging in without permission. I’m the manager here, but I kept getting complaints, so I had no choice but to use the master key—”
hunks.sol: “Hey, new guy. Sorry for barging in without asking. I’m the manager here, but the complaints kept coming, so I had to use the master key…”

hunks.baseline: The manager stared at my tear-streaked face, let his voice trail off, scratched his greasy hair, and closed the door.
hunks.sol: The manager took one look at my tear-streaked face and trailed off. He scratched his greasy hair, then closed the door.

hunks.baseline: I thought that the manager, who looked like some middle-aged man, would never come back.
hunks.sol: He looked like some middle-aged guy, and I figured he wouldn’t be back.

hunks.baseline: At least, not until I saw him again a little later, carrying soju and a bag of ramen in his hands.
hunks.sol: A little later, he returned with soju in one hand and a bag of ramen in the other.

hunks.baseline: “Want a drink? Oh, wait. You’re not a minor… obviously. Look at the size of you. Whew.”
hunks.sol: “Want a drink? Oh, wait. You’re not a minor… Obviously not. Look at the size of you. Whew.”

hunks.baseline: As time passed, I changed. My fear of monsters and the loneliness I felt being separated from my family gradually faded.
hunks.sol: Time passed, and I changed. My fear of monsters and the loneliness of being away from my family gradually faded.

hunks.baseline: No.
I became numb to them.
hunks.sol: No. I grew numb to them.

hunks.baseline: Like a hamster placed on a wheel, I simply ran and ran.
hunks.sol: Like a hamster on a wheel, I just kept running.

hunks.baseline: Even if I couldn’t move forward, it was better than stopping. There were things I could protect only by keeping that wheel turning.
hunks.sol: Even if I wasn’t getting anywhere, running was better than stopping. There were things I could protect only by keeping that wheel turning.

hunks.baseline: Family.
Friends.
hunks.sol: Family. Friends. Comrades.

hunks.baseline: Companions.
By then, I couldn’t stop anymore.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t stop anymore.

hunks.baseline: The tiny hamster wheel inside the cage that had confined me had, at some point, transformed into the enormous wheel of fate. And the word *duty* I carried in my heart had grown increasingly clear—and increasingly heavy.
hunks.sol: At some point, the little wheel in the cage that held me had become the enormous wheel of fate. And the word *duty*, which I carried in my heart, had grown clearer and heavier.

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why I had been able to look into that fading memory, if only in a dream.
hunks.sol: Why I had been able to revisit that fading memory, if only in a dream.

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why my cheeks had been wet when I opened my eyes to someone shaking me awake.
hunks.sol: Why my cheeks were wet when I opened my eyes to someone shaking me awake.

hunks.baseline: “…Gyeong. Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
hunks.sol: “…kyung. Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

hunks.baseline: I blinked. At last, my blurry vision came into focus.
hunks.sol: I blinked. My blurred vision finally came into focus.

hunks.baseline: The familiar face looking down at me with concern showed no noticeable change in expression. Perhaps because of that, even the smallest emotion stood out all the more.
hunks.sol: A familiar face looked down at me with concern. His expression had barely changed, which only made the small trace of emotion stand out more.

hunks.baseline: I rubbed the dampness from the corners of my eyes and answered.
hunks.sol: I rubbed my wet eyes and answered.

hunks.baseline: “Were you having a bad dream?”
hunks.sol: “Did you have a bad dream?”

hunks.baseline: “I couldn’t say.”
hunks.sol: “I’m not sure.”

hunks.baseline: I sat up, my voice hoarse.
Through the gap between the curtains hanging by the window, I could see the dark landscape outside. The clock showed that it had only just passed noon.
hunks.sol: I sat up, my voice hoarse. The clock showed that it was just past noon. Through a gap in the curtains, I could see how dark it was outside.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know whether it was a nightmare or a good dream. I don’t know either.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know if it was a bad dream or a good one. I really don’t.”

hunks.baseline: Team Leader Choi watched me in silence before speaking in a calm voice.
hunks.sol: Team Leader Choi watched me in silence before speaking calmly.

hunks.baseline: He was right. A dream was only a dream. People were the ones who determined whether something would bring good or bad fortune—and that was my role today.
hunks.sol: He was right. A dream was only a dream. Whether today brought good or bad fortune was up to us—and deciding that was my role.

hunks.baseline: No.
Our role.
hunks.sol: No. It was everyone’s.

hunks.baseline: “I haven’t fully woken up yet, so let me ask you something. Was what happened last night also a dream?”
hunks.sol: “I’m still half-asleep, so let me ask you something. Was last night a dream too?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. A lot of familiar faces appeared. At the end, I even saw a British prince dressed as a hotel bellboy.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. There were a lot of familiar faces. Toward the end, I even saw a British prince dressed as a hotel bellboy.”

hunks.baseline: Only then did a faint smile appear at the corners of Team Leader Choi’s mouth.
hunks.sol: Only then did a faint smile touch Team Leader Choi’s lips.

hunks.baseline: “Oh, you did? Personally, I thought it was a pretty nice dream.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, you did? Personally, I thought it was a pretty good one.”

hunks.baseline: “I thought so, too.”
hunks.sol: “So did I.”

hunks.baseline: Naturally, that part had not been a dream.
hunks.sol: That part, of course, hadn’t been a dream.

hunks.baseline: The conversation that had begun in secret had continued until deep into the night, and I had collapsed into sleep beneath the weight of the exhaustion I had accumulated over the past few days.
hunks.sol: Our secret conversation had gone on until the small hours of the morning. Worn out by the past few days, I’d fallen asleep as if I’d passed out.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps thanks to that, my mind was clear and my body felt light.
hunks.sol: Maybe that was why my mind felt clear and my body felt light.

hunks.baseline: Almost unnaturally so.
hunks.sol: Almost too light.

hunks.baseline: *Of course, there are a few flaws.*
hunks.sol: *There is one small problem, of course.*

hunks.baseline: I focused on the faint pain deep within my body.
hunks.sol: I focused on the faint pain deep inside me.

hunks.baseline: The effects of **Broken Body**, which had yet to be healed, were not merely represented as numbers on the System. Like a parasite clinging to its host, they were eating away at part of my strength.
hunks.sol: **Broken Body** still hadn’t healed. Its effects weren’t just numbers displayed by the System. Like a parasite clinging to a host, it was eating away at some of my strength.

hunks.baseline: *Can I do it? Even in this condition?*
hunks.sol: *Can I do it? Even like this?*

hunks.baseline: A single question flashed through my mind.
hunks.sol: The question flashed through my mind. I shook my head.

hunks.baseline: But I soon shook my head.
This was not a matter of whether I could do it or not.
hunks.sol: Whether I could do it wasn’t the question.

hunks.baseline: I had to do it.
hunks.sol: I had to.

hunks.baseline: For everyone—including me and my people.
hunks.sol: For me, for my people, and for everyone else.

hunks.baseline: “What about the preparations?”
hunks.sol: “Are we ready?”

hunks.baseline: The conviction in his voice was unmistakable—the attitude of someone who had prepared everything he possibly could.
hunks.sol: There was certainty in his voice—the kind that came from having done everything he could to prepare.

hunks.baseline: But I asked again.
Not Team Leader Choi, but another person crouching somewhere out of sight.
hunks.sol: But I asked again, this time addressing someone else, crouched somewhere out of sight.

hunks.baseline: “What about you?”
hunks.sol: “And you?”

hunks.baseline: Even though he had clearly seen and heard everything happening here, he chose silence once more.
As though he were someone trying to sever every last shred of affection between us. As though he were a traveler who had finished preparing to leave.
hunks.sol: He must have seen and heard everything, but he chose silence again. As though he were trying to cut away every last shred of affection between us. As though he were a traveler packed and ready to leave.

hunks.baseline: But…
I had no intention of letting him go.
hunks.sol: But… I had no intention of letting him go.

hunks.baseline: Especially not for some fucking reason like this.
hunks.sol: Especially not for a reason as fucked up as this.

hunks.baseline: I left the room in a calm voice.
Team Leader Choi followed immediately, and the Hunters from the Peace and Ares Guilds filled the hallway behind us, trailing after us like a dragon’s tail.
hunks.sol: I said it evenly and left the room. Team Leader Choi followed at once, and the Hunters of the Peace and Ares Guilds filled the corridor behind us, trailing like a dragon’s tail.

hunks.baseline: Dark clouds had spread across the capital region under cover of dawn, spilling a light drizzle, and the air against my skin was chilly.
hunks.sol: Dark clouds had spread across the capital region before dawn, bringing a light drizzle. The air felt chilly against my skin.

hunks.baseline: But to the people, the weather was irrelevant.
hunks.sol: But the weather meant nothing to the people.

hunks.baseline: They had hope that the clouds would soon scatter and sunlight would shine through.
hunks.sol: They expected the clouds to clear and the sun to shine through soon.

hunks.baseline: No.
Perhaps *conviction* was a more accurate word than hope.
hunks.sol: No. *Certainty* might have been a better word.

hunks.baseline: That was the sunlight everyone had been waiting for—the alliance of superhumans that would save them from the second Great War that was about to descend upon them, or perhaps had already begun.
hunks.sol: That was the sunlight they had been waiting for: an alliance of superhumans who would save them from the second Great War, soon to descend on them—or perhaps already begun.

hunks.baseline: The heroes of the past, present, and future would gather in one place and be reborn as Hunters in the truest sense of the word.

hunks.baseline: They would become humanity’s sword and shield, clearing away those dark clouds and protecting the world from the monsters surging in like waves.
hunks.sol: Heroes of the past, present, and future would gather in one place and become Hunters in the truest sense. They would be humanity’s sword and shield, drive away the dark clouds, and protect the world from the monsters surging in like waves.

hunks.baseline: *A new history begins.*
hunks.sol: *New history begins.*

hunks.baseline: Swish.
The enormous round table had three hundred seats, and its surface was covered in marks left by sharp weapons.
hunks.sol: The enormous round table had three hundred seats. Marks left by sharp weapons covered its surface.

hunks.baseline: *Records left behind by heroes.*
hunks.sol: *The marks the heroes left behind.*

hunks.baseline: He still remembered it clearly.
hunks.sol: He remembered that day clearly.

hunks.baseline: On the day the unprecedented alliance known as the World Hunter Federation was born, Michael Silbert had stood alongside them in that glorious moment.
hunks.sol: When the World Hunter Federation—an alliance unlike any before it—was born, Michael Silbert had been there to share in its glory.

hunks.baseline: Beside those who were now dead, he had shouted until his blood ran hot. They had drawn their weapons and pointed them at the sky, then driven their swords into the enormous round table and sworn to become humanity’s sword and shield.
hunks.sol: Beside men and women now long dead, he had shouted with his blood aflame. They had drawn their weapons and pointed them skyward, then driven their swords into the great round table and sworn to become humanity’s sword and shield.

hunks.baseline: It was an unforgettable memory.
hunks.sol: He could never forget it.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert gently stroked the chair where he had once sat.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert gently stroked the chair he had once occupied. Age had left it rough and creaking, yet even that stirred something in him.

hunks.baseline: It carried every mark left by the years. It was rough and creaked beneath his touch, but even that stirred a strange emotion within him.
But that was all.
hunks.sol: But only for a moment.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert merely looked down at the object that held his memories of the past. He did not sit in it or lean against it.
hunks.sol: He looked down at the chair that held those memories without sitting in it or leaning against it. His gaze drifted away from it, toward the center of the round table.

hunks.baseline: At some point, his gaze had left the chair and turned toward the center of the round table.
There was no chair there, nor any platform. Isolated by the three hundred seats, it almost seemed as desolate as an uninhabited island.
hunks.sol: There was no chair or platform there. Ringed by three hundred seats, it almost looked as desolate as an uninhabited island.

hunks.baseline: But in the past, neither Michael Silbert nor anyone else had thought of it that way.
hunks.sol: But neither Michael nor anyone else had thought so back then.

hunks.baseline: There had always been one person who filled that space.
hunks.sol: One man had always filled that space.

hunks.baseline: The strongest and brightest of them all. The hero among heroes, whom even those who envied him had no choice but to regard with awe and fear.
hunks.sol: Stronger and brighter than anyone else. A hero among heroes, whom even those who envied him could only regard with awe and fear.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert suddenly raised his head and looked around.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert raised his head and looked around.

hunks.baseline: The First National Assembly Hall, which had since become a World Heritage site.

hunks.baseline: Stained glass created just after the war ended, depicting the course of humanity’s victory in the Great Cataclysm, glittered on every side.
hunks.sol: The First National Assembly Hall had since become a World Heritage site. Stained glass installed just after the war, depicting humanity’s victory in the Great Cataclysm, glittered on every side.

hunks.baseline: Monsters and humans locked in fierce battle. Blood flowing like rivers, and corpses piled up in every direction…
hunks.sol: Humans and monsters locked in fierce battle. Blood flowing in rivers. Corpses piled everywhere…

hunks.baseline: His gaze passed over the traces of the old heroes who had etched their names into history with their dazzling accomplishments—heroes who, unfortunately, were now mostly dead.
hunks.sol: His gaze passed over the old heroes immortalized there by their dazzling feats, most of them now dead. Then it settled on the highest point in that glorious record.

hunks.baseline: Then it came to rest on one place.
The highest point within those glorious records.
The two figures carved into the ceiling.
hunks.sol: Two figures set into the ceiling.

hunks.baseline: *My, my. You’re still looking down at me from up there.*
hunks.sol: *Well. You’re still looking down at me from up there.*

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert let out a quiet laugh.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert gave a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: The savior who had driven a sword into the heart of Asmodeus, the Demon King who had cast humanity into a pit of flames, was looking down at him.
hunks.sol: The savior who had driven his sword into the heart of Asmodeus—the Demon King who had cast humanity into a pit of fire—looked down at him.

hunks.baseline: As though warning him never to forget his existence.
hunks.sol: As though warning Michael not to forget him.

hunks.baseline: As though he might descend at any moment and pass divine judgment like a god.
hunks.sol: As though he might descend at any moment and mete out divine punishment.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert smiled gently.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert smiled softly.

hunks.baseline: In his youth, he had been neither particularly strong nor particularly weak compared to the other heroes.
hunks.sol: In his youth, he had been neither particularly strong nor particularly weak beside the other heroes. Now he had returned, his strength beyond anyone’s denial.

hunks.baseline: Now, he had returned as a powerhouse no one could deny.
*But what about you?*
hunks.sol: *And what about you?*

hunks.baseline: Cheon Taemin—the man Michael had revered, feared, and been forced to keep his head down to avoid drawing attention from—was gone.
hunks.sol: Cheon Taemin—the man Michael had revered and feared, the man who had forced him to lie low for fear of attracting his notice—was gone.

hunks.baseline: All he could do now was remain as a record in this place and watch Michael, who would soon ascend the throne.
hunks.sol: All the savior of humanity could do now was remain a record in this hall and watch Michael ascend the throne.

hunks.baseline: That was all the savior of humanity could do.
“I’ll fill the place where you once stood.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll take the place where you once stood.”

hunks.baseline: And the moment those words left his mouth in a voice brimming with joy—
hunks.sol: The words came out full of elation.

hunks.baseline: The tightly closed door opened, and a voice seeped through the gap along with the light.
hunks.sol: The tightly shut door opened. Light spilled through the gap, along with a voice.
